title: Kernel scheduler jitter: mixed-quant exploration and notes
body:
Summary:

Quick notes from spike investigating unexplained latency variance ("jitter") when serving mixed-quant model variants (GPTQ/AWQ + FP8 emulation) on our production-like nodes. This doc captures the experimental matrix, raw profiler snippets, hypotheses about scheduler interactions, and short-term mitigations. Goal is to decide whether we need a kernel-aware request scheduler vs. tweak existing batch formation heuristics.

Why this matters:
- Intermittent p95 spikes during steady-state throughput hurt SLOs and user experience. Observed across both dedicated and hosted clusters.
- Spikes often correlate with model-variant switches (fallbacks, rollouts) where requests for different quant types hit same GPU.

Quick TL;DR observations:
- When mixing AWQ and GPTQ variants on the same worker, end-to-end latency p95 increased by 18-36% compared to homogeneous workloads, even when p50 stayed similar.
- GPU utilization appears stable, but SM scheduler metrics and kernel launch latencies show increased tail.
- Small batches (<4 tokens) are most affected due to kernel launch overhead differences between quant codepaths.

Experimental setup (short):
- Hardware: 8x A100s (40GB) on prod-like instance (single-process-per-GPU mode), CUDA 11.8, driver 535.xx.
- Runtime: rwinf/serving v2.3.4 feature/quant-scheduler-experiments branch.
- Models: llm-13b-v2 (GPTQ-4bit), llm-13b-awq (AWQ-4bit), baseline fp16 13b.
- Kernels: flash-attn-v2 (fused fp16), cutlass-matmul-quant (our int8 path), triton-vec-quant (AWQ fast path).
- Workload: synthetic prompt mix (50% short chat 8–24 tokens, 50% medium 64–128 tokens) with Poisson arrival to emulate PLG burstiness.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU SM activity, kernel launch latency from nvprof-like traces, runtime internal scheduling events (batch formation, queue depth), nvtx markers.

Profiler snippets (representative):
- trace excerpt (shortest form):
  [2024-10-11T18:23:12Z] req=0x7f3a: enqueue -> batch_form (wait 12ms) -> kernel_launch(cutlass) latency 2.1ms -> kernel_done -> kv-cache-copy 0.7ms -> response 14.5ms
  [2024-10-11T18:23:12Z] req=0x9b2: enqueue -> batch_form (wait 9ms) -> kernel_launch(triton_awq) latency 6.9ms -> kernel_done -> response 22.3ms
- Observed that triton_awq launch latency spikes to 4–8ms intermittently, while cutlass path stays 1.5–2.5ms.
- Kernel-level concurrency: when awq path launches, it blocks some fused kernels resulting in queuing inside CUDA stream groups; manifests as per-request jitter.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel launch / JIT compilation jitter: AWQ/triton path triggers codegen or memory allocation at first few uses in a lifetime, causing tail latency for those requests.
2) Mixed-kernel scheduling interference: different kernels have incompatible stream/priority patterns causing head-of-line blocking for small batches.
3) Memory pinning / small memcpy thrash: AWQ path performs extra tensors/pinned allocations which briefly affect PCIe bandwidth and cause small delays for subsequent kernels.
4) Lock contention in runtime's kernel registry for variant lookup when many model variants are loaded into the same process.

Evidence supporting hypotheses:
- Warm-start experiments: re-running same workload for 10 minutes reduces initial spikes but long-tail persists => not purely JIT.
- Synthetic microbench of kernel-launch-only (no host-side post-processing) reproduces 60% of observed launch latency variance => points to CUDA scheduling/streaming.
- NVTX group traces show sequence: triton_awq kernel -> small cudaMemcpyAsync -> cutlass kernel; memcpy occasionally delayed ~1–3ms.
- Runtime logs show short windows where lock-acquire times in registry spike concurrent with model-variant routing events.

Short-term mitigations tried and effect:
- Enforce affinity (one quant class per GPU): eliminates cross-variant interference but not feasible for low-util multi-tenant pools.
- Serialize small-batch AWQ launches with a micro-sleep (1ms): reduced p95 by ~8% but throughput suffered at high load.
- Pre-warm JIT/codegen at model load: removes first-minute cold spikes but not steady-state tail.

Root-cause working theory:
- Combination of kernel launch scheduling differences + occasional small async memcpy contention + sporadic lock contention in variant routing leads to observed jitter. Not a single root cause. Interactions amplify tail effects for small-batch, mixed-quant traffic.

Recommended medium-term actions (next 4–8 weeks):
1) Implement kernel-aware scheduling: annotate requests with "quant-class" and prefer batching/scheduling that keeps same-quant requests together for small-batch windows.  Estimated dev: 2w to prototype, 4w to stabilize.
2) Consolidate and refactor kernel registry to reduce lock granularity (move heavy ops to async init).  Estimated dev: 1–2w.
3) Add pinned-buffer pool and explicit pinned-memory budgeting to prevent transient memcpy stalls.  Estimated dev: 2w.
4) Instrument stream/priority usage in runtime to avoid interleaving incompatible kernels on same stream groups.  1w instrumentation, follow-up tuning TBD.

Experiment matrix (planned):
- Vars: batch_size {1,2,4,8}, mix_ratio {homog, 70/30, 50/50}, quant_pair {AWQ+FP16, GPTQ+AWQ, GPTQ+FP16}, kernel_set {cutlass+triton, flash-only, triton-only}, prewarm {yes/no}
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), SM occupancy distribution, kernel launch latency percentiles, memcpy latency distribution, runtime lock wait time percentiles.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do AWQ kernels trigger occasional device-side codegen in our triton builds? Need vendor/author confirmation. (action: Samir to ping triton maintainers / upstream PR references).
- Do different CUDA driver versions change the launch-tail behavior? Quick CI matrix across CUDA 11.5/11.8/12.0 recommended.
- Is there a cheap runtime heuristic (time-window coalescing) that captures most of the benefit of kernel-aware scheduling without full redesign? Prototype idea: 5ms sticky-quant window per GPU.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a lightweight spike doc — please call out if we should prioritize making scheduling changes vs. kernel refactor.
- See linked artifacts for raw traces and the branch with additional logging.

Action items (owner):
- Samir: create triton/cuda quick-test matrix and report by 2024-10-21.
- Olivia: prototype sticky-quant scheduler that biases batch formation for 5ms windows (P0 prototype due 2024-11-05).
- Maya: refactor kernel registry locks into async init; open RFC by 2024-10-18.

Appendix (raw probe sample lines):
- kernel-launch timings sample: [cutlass] 1.9ms, 2.0ms, 1.7ms, 2.2ms, [triton_awq] 5.1ms, 6.8ms, 4.7ms, 7.9ms
- memcpy async latency sample: 0.12ms, 0.14ms, 2.1ms, 0.13ms, 1.9ms
- runtime lock hold times (ms): 0.02, 0.03, 0.25, 0.01, 0.18

If you want raw traces or the small harness used to run microbenchmarks, pointed to the PR above.
